notation_findings.finding: Both ornate groupoid labels have the open curved lower body and upper return of C; retain C in both occurrences.
All live occurrences, including both ends of (*), were read separately. Their caps and upright legs support capital Pi; no notation change is proposed.
The separate doubled stem of N and the two-stroke plus remain clear; retain the current alphabet and exponent.
The target argument is juxtaposed f and x prime, with only the outer closing parenthesis; retain the absence of an inner parenthesis pair.
The raised mark remains ambiguous and must not become a settled notation rule. Two small points below-left of the Theta oval are incidental pen traces, not another mark to transcribe.

notes: The whole page and both existing native overlapping halves were each read once in full. All 27 inventoried elements are present and accounted for, including the author number 15, both slanted notes, their cancellations, the long separator drawing, and the lighter archive folio 94. No missing element was found.

The page continues an opening sentence and ends with an unfinished sentence followed by a comma. Neither end is completed editorially. The abbreviated autom, rev. and hom. and the visible insertion/deletion spans are retained.

The sole proposed correction is single rather than double underlining of un. It revises existing locus 095-37. C explicitly gives double underlining; H uses italic emphasis and is not substantively altered at this place.

The two tiny dark points directly below-left of the stable-sous Theta oval, approximately original x847–854/y1794–1808, were considered explicitly on star_map_lift. Their position beneath the glyph contour does not establish a word, punctuation, cancellation or independent annotation. They are excluded as incidental pen traces. Root reused the same crop and independently agreed; no colon or drawing is added.

All nine previously retained doubts remain unresolved after the second reading. The opening qui/que, upper cancelled ending, low cancelled prefix, overinked target Y/X, raised prime/star, marginal de, bornions/bornons and closing pense/peux are not repaired from grammatical or mathematical expectation; the cancelled groupoid sign likewise remains doubtful.

The manuscript states necessary conditions for an object-fixing groupoid automorphism to arise from a Galois element: lifts through finite étale coverings and invariance of kernels of induced maps, with a periodic-point power variant. This audit reads those statements and their qualifications; it performs no independent proof. The supplied first-reading targeted kernel-invariance check is not counted as a new event here.
Root’s later agreement on the underline and incidental traces is recorded separately from the auditor’s observations. No new crop, OCR, research, TeX compilation, or other page source was used.
